page.layout: One page of running text in one column, with the running head and page number at the top. No marginal notes. A bare numeral "XI." stands at the lower right below the last line.

main_text.p: Donatistam : citat pariter locum Paulinum ad Hebr. viii. 10. de novo Fœdere pangendo post illos dies, &c. Non quidem expresso Pauli Apostoli nomine, ut affirmat Baronius, sed eo haud obscurè notato.

IX. Hilarius, Episcopus Pictaviensis, Latinæ Eloquentiæ Rhodanus, clarus sub Constantio, mortuus Valentiniano & Valente regnantibus; Libr. iv. de Trinitate, Facturam autem, per id quod Paulus ad Hebræos dixerit. Tanto melior factus est Angelis &c. Hebr.1.4. Arianæ idem ille hæreseos profligator acerrimus, atque adeò Epistolæ vindex.

X. Gregorius Baeticus, Hiberi Episcopus, sub Valentiniano & Valente Imperatoribus; Libro de fide, Epistolam inducit ut Paulinam, Alibi docet Apostolus de Filio Dei esse scriptum. Et adorent eum omnes Angeli &c. Hebr.1.6. Quin & ipse à partibus Catholicorum contrà Arianos stetisse fertur, apud Eusebi[?]. Chronicorum Libr. poster. in Valentiniano & Valente. Torserit ergo in Arianos egregia, quæ Epistola suppeditat, argumenta.

page.notes: The running head is italic "ad Hebræos." and the page number 169 is printed at the upper right. The word after "apud" is a doubtful reading ("Eusebi" with a bold stop, possibly "Eusebii"). The ligature in "Pictaviensis" and the mixed italic in "Hebr.1.4." and "Hebr.1.6." are reproduced as far as the scan allows. "XI." is treated as a bare numeral, not a heading or catchword.
